subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw implement #49251 as a core-owned durable provider-capacity prompt queue, or keep only the narrower provider cooldown and followup-restart mitigations?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses provider failover, session suspension, channel delivery, queue persistence, user-visible status, and replay semantics, so the permanent product boundary and interaction with open partial PRs need maintainer intent before an autonomous repair PR.

options.title: Design one durable capacity queue
options.body: Approve a core SQLite-backed queue/replay design and use the related PRs only if they fit that single path.

options.title: Land only partial mitigations
options.body: Keep #49251 open but limit near-term work to provider cooldown and followup restart persistence without promising durable prompt replay.

options.title: Reject durable replay
options.body: Close the request as too risky or out of scope and rely on visible failure/cooldown status plus user re-prompting.

recommendation.title: Design one durable capacity queue
recommendation.body: Approve a core SQLite-backed queue/replay design and use the related PRs only if they fit that single path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history and the broad runtime/provider/session ownership signals point to steipete as the best available owner for the cross-cutting product decision.
